policy: Resolve exact historical parent text through every canonical ordinary/delayed child. Preserve source, independent and physical clauses; a compiled alternative never becomes a physical result.

topics.T54.04: The model injects publication at mask/clear/rearm/final-check boundaries; actual per-bank HSEM ownership and bounded budget/runnable paths distinguish lost wakeups. Arrival3/service2 has unbounded backlog, while burst3/arrival1/service2 has an explicit finite bound. Physical delivery is retained as a separate gate.
topics.T54.05: Line-rounded dirty-neighbor and speculative-refill counterexamples compose actual Pd preclean/invalidate/release/completion/acquire operations. Cached images isolate control and payload regions and initialize selected cache hardware. Cross-build/model evidence is kept separate from physical stale-data observations.
topics.T54.06: Two disjoint buffers compose actual Pd/Xd lease, selected DMA2 registers and cache boundaries; DEVICE ownership persists through late writes and stale tokens. TE quiescence permits release without success publication. Target reachability rules and physical completion observations remain distinct.
topics.T54.07: Calibration/clock-domain and wrap arguments, same-core roundtrip computation, synthetic distribution and changed burst workload are explicitly bound. Raw board calibration, external timing and universal WCET remain unobserved rather than inferred from native/QEMU clocks.
topics.T54.08: Supervisor-owned receipt, conflicting/stale command refusal, preserved epoch ledger and controlled park/quiet restart implement application reconciliation. Full power loss does not preserve the in-memory receipt; unexpected reset fails closed and physical hardware recovery remains unobserved.
topics.T54.09: The actual bounded acquisition/task pipeline uses2/4/8 queues, explicit burst/backpressure and per-ID completed/rejected/uncertain ledgers. Model costs and real target instruction costs are different inputs; changed core placement/interference is measured only in the declared environment.
topics.T54.10: Separate source-bound image/map/stack/command dossiers,512-ID pipeline and local-compute variant support author reproducibility. The structured physical capture protocol is authored, but physical load/restart/cache-DMA execution and independent assessment remain required events.
topics.T55.01: Forward and reverse release/acquire chains,2048 wrapped histories, translated counter-width model, early publication/reuse controls and actual pinned-CPU equal-workload layout measurements address ordering/stress/cost work. Finite races absent on one machine are not a portable proof.
topics.T55.02: The checked counter handles injected spurious failures, stale expected values and exhaustion; a repeatable1024-round starvation prefix distinguishes whole-call progress. Actual unpublished-ticket cancellation requires owner acknowledgement; allocator/libatomic dependencies remain in the progress argument.
topics.T55.03: Exact reuse histories and full-incarnation identity checks distinguish stale CAS from a numeric tag alone. Raw pointers require a live protected owner; nonwrapping generation retirement trades availability for stale-authority exclusion.
topics.T55.04: FREE/RESERVED/LINKED/RETIRED accounting, failed-link ownership, bounded cancellation and actual skewed per-thread/shared/stealing pool experiments resolve whole-operation exhaustion. Stopped participants change who can perform work; four holders are not silently replaced with a fifth actor.
topics.T55.05: Actual publication/revalidation, paused collector incarnation, finite retirement, stale registration and hazard-versus-epoch retention comparisons supply the expanded schedules. SC cycle reasoning is explicitly not transferred to release/acquire scans without synchronization.
topics.T55.06: Actual paused publishers/dequeuers exercise helping and protected old dummy lifetime. Threaded40000-value execution and independent67500-case FIFO/pending-history checker retain interval witnesses; neither is a proof over all schedules.
topics.T55.07: Concrete append/read/remove retired-list integration binds entry/exit quiescence and stopped participants. Progress and retention are assessed under exact participant and departure premises, with later safe cleanup distinguished from unsafe forced reuse.
topics.T55.08: Concrete immutable payload/version slots and reclamation measurements replace bare epoch metadata. Version overflow/finite capacity and copied versus borrowed snapshot costs remain explicit rather than promising unlimited publication.
topics.T55.09: Pending operations, completions and real-time intervals are checked against an independently derived sequential specification. Actual trace/witness replay and negative histories address checker sensitivity; a bounded accepted history is not algorithm-wide linearizability.
topics.T55.10: Equal payload/capacity/completion contracts and raw repeats compare mutex, SPSC and MPMC paths, including allocator/reclamation and stopped participant effects. Central-loop lock freedom is never substituted for whole-path progress or a universal speedup.
topics.T56.01: Actual original guest process/TCB ownership, cancellation and quiescent reaping classify process/thread identities and references across exit. Dead owners do not imply device-owned storage can already be reused.
topics.T56.02: Actual guest ELF/frame/page-table/handle acquisition failures unwind the complete process construction graph. Portable rollback remains useful but is no longer the only evidence for target cleanup and publication order.
topics.T56.03: Actual guest demand-zero/OOM attribution and frame-ledger checks separate user failure from kernel invariants and first-touch materialization. Concurrent fault recheck prevents two frames from publishing to one mapping.
topics.T56.04: Actual COW page tables, references, copy/sole-owner paths and target invalidation-before-resume distinguish logical copy admission from completed remote translation cleanup. Retained storage is accounted until those acknowledgements.
topics.T56.05: Actual protected channel lookup, directional rights, stable copied user spans and waiter close/cancellation provide syscall-boundary evidence; failed copy does not consume the retained message or advance ownership.
topics.T56.06: Actual shared-object grants, read-only mappings, unmap and close references make independent mapping lifetime and synchronization visible. A common physical page does not grant write authority or define a protocol by itself.
topics.T56.07: The explicit two-request virtio successor changes from IRQ-plus-used progress to used-ring polling, accumulates two completions, acknowledges each matching waiter and retains buffers through timeout/reset uncertainty. Actual131074 reads cross16-bit indices twice; this is not a physical-disk durability claim.
topics.T56.08: Actual archive parsing and guest open/dup/read/seek/close use independent opens versus shared duplicate offsets, checked spans, preserved offsets on copy failure and fixed byte hashes. The extended seek policy is versioned and does not silently rewrite the retained SDK contract.
topics.T56.09: Actual bytecode request identities, fuel, pending result/cancel, client copy boundaries and multi-client progress compose the retained VM service. No disk capability is inferred from the existence of an interpreter or a host-side model.
topics.T56.10: Actual retained-store transaction and client session/receipt handling, disposable guest disk flush/cut cases and no-reapply high-water policy replace the portable-only service limitation. Explicit flush/sector assumptions delimit durability.
topics.T56.11: Actual write/reboot/verify42 versus fresh-file zero control, owner endpoint/session replacement and inactive-commit WAL cuts resolve restart evidence. Orphaned pending I/O retains device ownership; eviction refuses stale IDs instead of reapplying effects.
topics.T56.12: Actual selected role images, equal offered workload and cache/DMA/restart/overload source-bound adapters supply author decomposition support. Full physical H745 service execution and external timing remain unperformed; the package preserves the capture gate.
